thread:
ravi: Throwing a different pattern on the table: what if operator uses an escrowed-credit model instead of explicit placement/grants? operator mints an escrow record (credits reserved) and runtime does a lightweight claim/reconcile flow. Operator keeps the ledger; runtime picks variants. Thoughts?
olga: Hmm. Escrowed credits could simplify rebalances if operator doesn't need to specify polices per-pool. But failure modes?
mike: Main win: operator stays declarative (reserve X credits for tenant), runtime gets to optimize variant selection and batching. Win for runtime latency control.
priya: Needs clear reclaim semantics. If operator needs capacity back, we need a safe revoke/settle protocol so inflight requests don't lose work. Also accounting must be correct.
tara: Proposal for lifecycle: reserve -> claim -> consume -> reconcile -> settle. Claim is idempotent and returns a provisional receipt. Reconcile is periodic so the operator can close ledger windows.
ops-bot: Alert: last week several tenants had unexpected quality drops during a scale event. Incident 6999900012 investigation attached: https://incidents/6999900012 :warning:
ravi: Good catch. Two safety knobs: immutable safety_flags attached to escrow (e.g., "no-quant", "max-latency-ms:1000"), and a revoke_grace window where operator marks escrow as draining but honors claims until grace expires.
olga: Can we sketch minimal API? I'd like to see claim/consume/reconcile endpoints and expected idempotency guarantees.
mike: Quick proto sketch (very small):
```
EscrowRecord {
  escrow_id: string
  tenant_id: string
  reserved_units: int64
  safety_flags: string[]  // e.g. ["no-quant", "min-precision:0.92"]
  revoke_at?: int64       // operator can set to start draining
}

ClaimRequest { escrow_id, request_id, wanted_units }
ClaimResponse { accepted_units, provisional_receipt }

Consume { provisional_receipt, used_units }
Reconcile { escrow_id, upto_ts }
```
priya: Important semantics: provisional_receipt must be unique+tamperproof (signed by operator) so runtime retries don't double-burn reserved_units. Also operator must persist consumes before ack or use a consistent ledger backend.
tara: Observability: runtime emits per-escrow metrics: accepted_units_by_variant, fallback_count, revoke_crossings, request_id traces. Operator surfaces per-escrow accounting and reconciliation diffs so finance matches usage.
ops-bot: FYI autoscaler noted ephemeral headroom exhaustion at 02:44 UTC affecting 6% of dedicated pools. Monitoring ticket: https://monitoring/alerts/6999997001 :information_source:
olga: Edgecases: 1) leader failover while provisional_receipt accepted but not persisted — need server-side dedupe and reconciliation window; 2) long-lived requests that cross revoke_at must be honored until revoke_at+grace.\n
mike: Also: runtime must expose a per-tenant fallback contract: what it will do when credits are low (e.g., degrade logits, trim history, cheaper model family). That contract should be surfaced by operator in tenant metadata so product teams know expected behavior.
priya: Contract idea: include a small "fallback_profile" string on escrow that enumerates allowed degradations. If operator sets "no-quant" and fallback_profile="none" then runtime must error rather than silently degrade.
ravi: Rollout plan: 1) build escrow ledger + provisional receipts in operator; 2) runtime implements claim/consume/reconcile handlers and emits metrics; 3) start advisory mode where runtime treats safety_flags as hints; 4) canary tenants flip to enforced mode; 5) full rollout with reconciliation dashboards.
ara: (typo) tara: small nit: include a versioned protocol field so we can evolve receipts without breaking.
priya: Good call. receipts should include proto_version and signature. Also define error codes: ESCROW_EXPIRED, INSUFFICIENT_RESERVED, VIOLATES_SAFETY, RECEIPT_INVALID.
ops-bot: Note: follow-up meeting scheduled for tomorrow 10:30 to review proto draft and reconciliation dashboard. Calendar invite: https://calendar/meet/6999998000 :white_check_mark:
ravi: Thanks everyone. I'll prototype a minimal operator escrow swagger and post PR. priya you want to own the runtime stubs?
priya: Yep, I'll start the stub and add unit tests for idempotency semantics.
mike: I'll draft the fallback_profile options and a short doc for product teams.
olga: I'll pair with priya on the reconciliation dashboard queries.
tara: SGTM. See you tomorrow. :rocket:
